entries.task_id: but eventually|spread|in the 1820s and 1830s to eastern polynesia
entries.description: but eventually spread in the 1820s and 1830s to Eastern Polynesia
entries.subject: but eventually
entries.object: in the 1820s and 1830s to Eastern Polynesia

spans.text: It was spoken mostly within Hawai‘i but eventually spread in the 1820s and 1830s to Eastern Polynesia, Tonga, and California; it also contributed lexically to Eskimo pidgins in Alaska (Drechsel & Makuakane 1982; van der Voort 1997).

entries.task_id: pidgin hawaiian|stabilized|as a language grammatically distinct from vernacular hawaiian
entries.description: Pidgin Hawaiian stabilized as a language grammatically distinct from vernacular Hawaiian
entries.subject: Pidgin Hawaiian
entries.object: as a language grammatically distinct from vernacular Hawaiian

spans.text: It was at this time when Pidgin Hawaiian stabilized as a language grammatically distinct from vernacular Hawaiian.

entries.subject:
of
Hawaiian

spans.text: Although the first instance of Hawaiian contact with Westerners occurred in 1778, sporadic and seasonal visits by Euroamerican explorers and fur traders did not commence until the late 1780s.

entries.task_id: i|served|as a convenient port-of-call for resupplying ships on trans-pacific and arctic voyages
entries.description: i served as a convenient port-of-call for resupplying ships on trans-Pacific and Arctic voyages
entries.subject: i
entries.object: as a convenient port-of-call for resupplying ships on trans-Pacific and Arctic voyages

spans.text: At the time Hawai‘i served as a convenient port-of-call for resupplying ships on trans-Pacific and Arctic voyages.

entries.task_id:
such
visits|were|intermittent and few in number
entries.description:
such
visits were intermittent and few in number
entries.subject:
such
visits

spans.text: Though such visits were intermittent and few in number, most occurred in the same locales (primarily Kealakekua, Hawai‘i, and Waimea, Kaua‘i) and relied on a small pool of native Hawaiian and non-native interpreters (Schütz 1994).

entries.task_id: of hawaiian|unmistakably|related to later pidgin hawaiian
entries.description: of Hawaiian unmistakably related to later Pidgin Hawaiian
entries.subject: of Hawaiian

spans.text: The linguistic abilities of two settlers, Elliot de Castro and Archibald Campbell, are fortuitously preserved in early sources (Campbell 1816; von Chamisso 1856), which show that they spoke simplified varieties of Hawaiian unmistakably related to later Pidgin Hawaiian.

entries.task_id: hawaiian features|were|recorded in 1789
entries.description: Hawaiian features were recorded in 1789
entries.subject: Hawaiian features

spans.text: In fact, the first Pidgin Hawaiian features (specifically pi mai ‘come’ and nuinui ‘a lot, many’) were recorded in 1789, barely 11 years after first contact (Martínez 1789).

entries.task_id: and euroamericans|intensified|in the 1830s and 1840s
entries.description: and Euroamericans intensified in the 1830s and 1840s
entries.subject: and Euroamericans

spans.text: Contact between Hawaiians and Euroamericans intensified in the 1830s and 1840s; whaling ships brought increasing numbers of foreigners to Hawaiian ports, the Hawaiian population in towns such as Honolulu began to swell as a consequence of economic dispossession, and many Hawaiians joined the crews of whaling ships as sailors.

entries.task_id: and english|were|spoken in hawai‘i during this period
entries.description: and English were spoken in Hawai‘i during this period
entries.subject: and English
entries.object: spoken in Hawai‘i during this period

spans.text: Documentary evidence shows that simplified varieties of both Hawaiian and English were spoken in Hawai‘i during this period, including a mixture of the two languages.

entries.task_id: while munger|recalled|his own acquisition of hawaiian aboard a whaling ship
entries.description: while Munger recalled his own acquisition of Hawaiian aboard a whaling ship
entries.subject: while Munger
entries.object: his own acquisition of Hawaiian aboard a whaling ship

spans.text: Jarman (1838: 124) alluded to the acquisition of Hawaiian by Anglophone sailors visiting Honolulu, while Munger (1852: 63–64) recalled his own acquisition of Hawaiian aboard a whaling ship.

entries.task_id: pidgin english|were|attested as early as the 1790s (roberts 2005)
entries.description: Pidgin English were attested as early as the 1790s (Roberts 2005)
entries.subject: Pidgin English

spans.text: Simplified varieties of English related to later Hawai‘i Pidgin English and general Pacific Pidgin English developed alongside Pidgin Hawaiian and the first features linked to later Hawai‘i Pidgin English (zero copula and future marker by and by) were attested as early as the 1790s (Roberts 2005).

entries.task_id: in 1876|made|the exportation of sugar profitable
entries.description: in 1876 made the exportation of sugar profitable
entries.subject: in 1876

spans.text: The ratification of the Reciprocity Treaty with the United States in 1876 made the exportation of sugar profitable, precipitating a large migration of contract labour.

entries.task_id: 000 chinese|entered|hawai‘i between 1877 and 1897
entries.description: 000 Chinese entered Hawai‘i between 1877 and 1897
entries.subject: 000 Chinese

spans.text: According to Reinecke (1969: 52, 55) and Takaki (1983: 45), over 37,000 Chinese entered Hawai‘i between 1877 and 1897, about 10,000 Portuguese from Madeira and the Azores arrived between 1878 and 1887, and over 200,000 Japanese immigrated between 1885 and 1924 as plantation labourers.

entries.task_id: that hawaiians|made|up 13
entries.description: that Hawaiians made up 13
entries.subject: that Hawaiians

spans.text: Plantation censuses published in immigration reports show that Hawaiians made up 13.7% of the workforce in 1888, and the percentage dropped to 6.1% a decade later.

entries.task_id: pidgin hawaiian|stabilized|as the prevailing contact medium
entries.description: Pidgin Hawaiian stabilized as the prevailing contact medium
entries.subject: Pidgin Hawaiian

spans.text: It was in the last quarter of the 19th century when Pidgin Hawaiian stabilized as the prevailing contact medium.

entries.task_id: primary interethnic|contact|medium on plantations and elsewhere
entries.description: primary interethnic contact medium on plantations and elsewhere
entries.subject: primary interethnic

spans.text: In the 1880s and 1890s Pidgin Hawaiian served as the primary interethnic contact medium on plantations and elsewhere.

entries.task_id: 1910s it|had|largely replaced pidgin hawaiian as general lingua franca
entries.description: 1910s it had largely replaced Pidgin Hawaiian as general lingua franca
entries.subject: 1910s it
entries.object: largely replaced Pidgin Hawaiian as general lingua franca

spans.text: Gradually Hawai‘i Pidgin English began to displace Pidgin Hawaiian on plantations and by the 1910s it had largely replaced Pidgin Hawaiian as general lingua franca.

entries.task_id: pidgin hawaiian|was|the language of the fields
entries.description: Pidgin Hawaiian was the language of the fields
entries.subject: Pidgin Hawaiian

spans.text: Jones (1942: 96, 176) similarly noted that in the 1880s “Pidgin Hawaiian was the language of the fields, and many of the Portuguese, both men and women, became adept in its usage.”

entries.task_id: a german|overseer|at kekaha sugar company (located in waimea
entries.description: a German overseer at Kekaha Sugar Company (located in Waimea
entries.subject: a German
entries.object: at Kekaha Sugar Company (located in Waimea

spans.text: For example, a Japanese immigrant was beaten to death in 1892 by a German overseer at Kekaha Sugar Company (located in Waimea, Kaua‘i), and court testimony shows that the immigrant, the overseer, the German assistant manager, and the plantation doctor all used Pidgin Hawaiian in cross-ethnic conversation.

entries.task_id: native hawaiians|comprised|only 2
entries.description: native Hawaiians comprised only 2
entries.subject: native Hawaiians

spans.text: In that year native Hawaiians comprised only 2.2% of the Kekaha workforce, so the general use of Pidgin Hawaiian was not due to accommodation to native speakers.
